name: Vasant Sridhar
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Strategy Officer, OfBusiness (OFB Tech), Gurugram
profile: Vasant Sridhar co-founded OfBusiness in 2015 with Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra and others. The Gurugram company runs B2B commerce for raw materials and SME financing (through its lending arm Oxyzo) and is valued at about $5B. He serves as Co-Founder and CSO.
interesting_fact: OfBusiness's team page lists him as a B.Tech graduate of IIT Madras who came to OfBusiness from ITC.
deep_cut_fact: Before OfBusiness he worked at the FMCG conglomerates ITC and Unilever, per his company and org-chart profiles.

public_contacts.value: https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/news (Press & Media page; PR lead Akansha Verma, VP PR & Corporate Communications, listed without email)

notes: Low public profile. Sources disagree on whether CSO means Chief Strategy or Chief Sales Officer. Best route is via OfBusiness's PR/corporate communications team.

name: Dheeraj Koneru
current_role: Co-Founder & SVP, Global Product Sales, Zenoti (Bellevue, WA / Hyderabad)
profile: Dheeraj Koneru co-founded Zenoti in 2010 with his brother Sudheer, who is CEO. Zenoti makes cloud management software for salons, spas, med spas and fitness businesses and is valued at about $2B. Dheeraj leads global product sales and drove the company's international expansion, including into fitness and gym management.
interesting_fact: Zenoti began as software he built in-house for the brothers' own Hyderabad chain, Latitudes Health Club and Tangerine Spas, after finding no suitable product on the market.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in particle physics from Cornell. He also co-founded Intelliprep Technologies, which later merged with Click2Learn, and held roles at Microsoft and SumTotal Systems.
notes: Some aggregators (Latka) wrongly list Dheeraj as CEO; per Zenoti, Sudheer Koneru is CEO. The Oct 2026 media contact is Dawn Cassidy at press@zenoti.com.

name: Brandon Woodward
current_role: Co-founder, TaxBit (Taxbit); current day-to-day role not confirmed
profile: Brandon Woodward co-founded TaxBit in Utah in 2017 with his cousins Austin Woodward (CEO) and Justin Woodward. TaxBit started as crypto tax software and now provides tax compliance and information-reporting software for digital assets and the gig economy. It raised $130M at a $1.33B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: TechCrunch reported that brothers Austin and Justin Woodward founded TaxBit with their cousin Brandon in 2017. The family team paired CPAs and tax attorneys with software developers from day one.
notes: Very low public profile; secondary sources describe his background as front-end development and design, but I couldn't confirm that from a primary source. Releases carry media contacts (media@/press@taxbit.com, agency Wachsman), but none could be confirmed on a fetched page, so none are listed. Best route is via the company or CEO Austin Woodward.

name: Karol Sobczak
current_role: Co-founder, Starburst Data; Trino open-source maintainer (current Starburst role unconfirmed)
profile: Karol Sobczak is a Warsaw-based database engineer and a co-founder of Starburst. Starburst commercialises the Trino (formerly PrestoSQL) distributed SQL query engine and is valued at about $3B. The company grew out of the Hadapt team, which Teradata acquired, and its engineering was rooted in Warsaw, Poland.
interesting_fact: Starburst's founding engineering team was based in Warsaw, Poland. It came from the Hadapt startup, which Teradata acquired, and had worked on developing Presto, the precursor to Trino.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the officially listed Trino project maintainers, under GitHub handle 'sopel39', alongside Presto/Trino creators Dain Sundstrom, David Phillips and Martin Traverso.
notes: Engineer-founder with a low media profile. A third-party profile (Stackforce) says his Starburst tenure ran Nov 2017 to Jul 2024, but this is unverified, so check whether he is still at Starburst. Possible warm route is the Trino community (Slack/GitHub).

name: Mahmoud Arram
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Bluecore (acquired by Insider One, May 2026); post-acquisition role unconfirmed
profile: Mahmoud Arram co-founded Bluecore in New York in 2013 with CEO Fayez Mohamood and Max Bennett, and serves as its CTO. Bluecore built AI-driven retail marketing and customer-identity technology for large retailers and reached a valuation of about $1B. Insider One acquired the company in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Bluecore came after four years of failed consumer products by the founders and grew out of a technical insight from one of their earlier projects. Arram first met CEO Fayez Mohamood in a freshman calculus class.
deep_cut_fact: He has said cooking gives him the same satisfaction as coding. He has also said Bluecore stuck with Python 'because it's what we were familiar with in the early days.'

public_contacts.value: christopher.baldwin@useinsider.com (Insider One VP Marketing, media contact for the Bluecore acquisition)

notes: Bluecore was acquired by Insider One (announced May 13, 2026), and Arram's current role there is not public. The acquisition is a good timely hook.

name: Silvio Kutic
profile: Silvio Kutić co-founded Infobip in 2006 in Vodnjan, Croatia, with Izabel Jelenić (CTO) and his brother Roberto (COO), and is its CEO. Infobip is a global cloud communications (CPaaS) platform that handles SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice messaging for businesses. Its $200M raise from One Equity Partners in 2020 made it Croatia's first unicorn.
interesting_fact: Infobip built a 17,000 m² campus, 'Pangea', in his small Istrian hometown of Vodnjan in 2017, followed by the 20,000 m² Alpha Centauri campus in Zagreb in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He lasted four hours in his first real job at the state power company in Zagreb, left for lunch, never returned, and took the bus home to Vodnjan. In 2003 his idea sent about 14,000 Christmas text greetings from Vodnjan's town hall to its emigrant community.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO; he was the guest on episode 1 of Infobip's ScaleUp & Up podcast ('Turning a $27,000 loan into a billion dollar company'). Infobip stayed bootstrapped for almost a decade. He fits a data-center/infrastructure angle via telecom APIs. Route through the Infobip global PR team (contacts from the Infobip media kit).

name: Christoph F. Gamon
current_role: Co-founder, Razor Group (Berlin), formerly CFO; current role unconfirmed
profile: Christoph Felix Gamon is listed as a co-founder (and former CFO) of Razor Group, founded in Berlin in 2020. Razor buys and scales Amazon marketplace (FBA) brands and was valued at $1.7B after merging with Perch in 2024. It merged with Infinite Commerce in August 2025. By then Max Biller was CEO and Jörg Meiner was CFO.
interesting_fact: Razor merged with US rival Perch in 2024, raising $100M at a $1.7B valuation. It then merged with Infinite Commerce in 2025 to form a Berlin- and Boston-headquartered FBA consolidator.

public_contacts.value: Gaffney Bennett PR (Avery Gerber), media contact on the Aug 2025 Razor/Infinite Commerce merger release (email obfuscated on page)

notes: Very low public profile. His founder/CFO role comes only from MarketScreener insider data (https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/CHRISTOPH-FELIX-GAMON-A1R4OS/), which also links him to Flash Ventures (Rocket Internet) and ConCloud GmbH. The 2025 releases do not name him, and CFO is now Jörg Meiner. Razor's own site was unreachable.

name: Dave Nicholson
current_role: Serial fintech founder and venture builder (London); listed as Chief Product Officer at Agricarbon (unverified profile)
profile: David Nicholson co-founded Zopa, the UK's first peer-to-peer lender and now a digital bank, in 2004-05 with fellow ex-Egg colleagues James Alexander and Richard Duvall, plus Giles Andrews and Tim Parlett. He left Zopa in 2007. In 2013 he co-founded the mobile payments and loyalty fintech Yoyo Wallet in London with Michael Rolph and Alain Falys.
interesting_fact: Zopa co-founder Giles Andrews has credited Nicholson with coming up with the idea that became Zopa. Nicholson came from a group of former consultants who had left Egg, the UK's first online bank.
deep_cut_fact: Zopa was pitched internally as an 'eBay for money' by its three ex-Egg co-founders, Nicholson, James Alexander and Richard Duvall, before they brought in Giles Andrews to raise money.
notes: He left Zopa in 2007 (https://alternativecreditinvestor.com/2020/04/28/where-are-they-now-the-p2p-lending-giants-still-run-by-their-founding-members/), so contact via Zopa is not appropriate. His current role at Agricarbon comes from an unverified theorg.com profile. No published contact found; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: William Addy
current_role: Founder and board member, ISN Software Corporation (Dallas, TX)
profile: Bill Addy founded Dallas-based ISN Software in 2001. ISN runs the ISNetworld platform, which energy, steel, pharma and other enterprises use to manage contractor and supplier compliance; it served 75,000+ customers in 85+ countries including 170 Fortune 500 firms. He was CEO until about 2015 and then executive chairman. ISN now lists him as Founder, with Brian Callahan as CEO. He is a Dallas philanthropist (The Addy Foundation).
interesting_fact: He and his wife Lydia gave the gift behind Addy Hall, a dormitory in Princeton's new residential colleges. Addy is a Princeton '82 chemical engineering graduate.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012 the Addys created the Addy/ISN North American Low Carbon Emission Energy Self-Sufficiency Fund at Princeton for research on cutting carbon and achieving North American energy self-sufficiency. His senior thesis was 'one part chemical engineering and nine parts economics' on ExxonMobil in western Colorado.
notes: A strong fit for an energy podcast: his clients are heavily energy-sector and he funds low-carbon energy research. Blackstone is an ISN investor with a board seat. He also does North Texas philanthropy (search results tie him to KERA public broadcasting, unverified). No published personal email.

name: Shiran Holtzman Erel
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Product Officer and board member, ODDITY Tech (NASDAQ: ODD; IL MAKIAGE, SpoiledChild)
profile: Shiran Holtzman Erel co-founded ODDITY with her brother, CEO Oran Holtzman. ODDITY is an Israeli-American, AI- and data-driven beauty and wellness company that owns IL MAKIAGE and SpoiledChild and listed on Nasdaq in 2023. She has been Chief Product Officer since inception and joined the board in November 2022.
interesting_fact: In 2013 she and her brother bought the struggling IL MAKIAGE brand out of receivership for NIS 12M plus NIS 80M of assumed debt, and turned it into a billion-dollar online beauty brand.
deep_cut_fact: She told Calcalist in 2020: 'In Israel, we're a proud retail player; in the U.S., we're 100% online.' This describes IL MAKIAGE's dual model of physical stores at home and a pure-online US business.
notes: Her brother Oran is the public face; she rarely gives interviews. ODDITY runs a biotech lab in Boston (ODDITY LABS) and an R&D centre in Tel Aviv, which could be an AI/data angle. Route through press@oddity.com.
